text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Authorities are pressuring dentists to reduce costs.

- In the first six months of the year some 230 people died in traffic accidents in Sweden, up from 220 at the same time one year ago. However, the number of deaths in traffic accidents in the past 30 years has fallen considerably.
- Mobile telephones helped lift Ericsson's half-year profit by 44 percent.
- Fast growth in the mobile telephone sector is the main reason Ericsson posted a half-year profit one billion crowns above market expectations.
- Danish municipalities pay Sweden some 1.6 million crowns to incinerate their rubbish.
- Swedish companies are planning measures to win over private investors by offering minimal fees for buying and selling shares.
- The market capitalisation of telcoms group AB LM Ericsson rose 23.5 billion crowns after the company posted a 6.1 billion crown pre-tax profit, exceeding expectations.
- Volvo and ABB are two Swedish companies which have been affected by the flooding in Poland. Damages have been minimal, however.
